stories.title: New Mexico court orders Meta to pay additional $567M in child safety case
stories.simple_summary: A court ordered Meta (Facebook and Instagram's company) to pay an additional $567 million for not protecting children safely on their platforms. This brings their total fine in this case to $942 million.
stories.why_it_matters: This shows that even huge tech companies face serious consequences for safety failures — it reminds us to be cautious about what our kids do online and which apps we trust them with.

stories.title: OpenAI’s new AI smart speaker will reportedly sell for between $300 and $400
stories.simple_summary: OpenAI is making a new smart speaker device that will cost between $300 and $400. It's a piece of technology you talk to, similar to Alexa or Google Home.
stories.why_it_matters: This is mostly important to investors and tech enthusiasts — most people already have affordable smart speakers, so you don't need to rush out and buy this.

stories.title: Jony Ive’s first OpenAI gadget is reportedly a hockey puck-sized smart speaker
stories.simple_summary: OpenAI is designing a small, battery-powered smart speaker with famous Apple designer Jony Ive. It's about the size of a hockey puck and is expected to come out in 2027 for over $300.
stories.why_it_matters: This is mostly news for investors and tech watchers — nothing you need to act on right now since it won't be available for several more years.

stories.title: Suno shares plans to combat spammy AI music
stories.simple_summary: Suno, a company that uses AI to create music, is adding a watermark (like a hidden stamp) to its songs to prove they were made by AI and stop low-quality spam music from spreading everywhere.
stories.why_it_matters: This shows AI music companies are trying to be more responsible and transparent — if you encounter AI-made music, you'll be able to tell it's artificial.

stories.title: ChatGPT brings unlimited text chats to free users
stories.simple_summary: OpenAI is letting free ChatGPT users chat with the AI as much as they want without hitting limits. They're also adding a button to help with complicated questions.
stories.why_it_matters: If you use ChatGPT for free, you can now use it more without running into annoying restrictions.

stories.title: Naïve raises $28.5M to automate the grunt work of setting up and running a company
stories.simple_summary: A company called Naïve raised $28.5 million to create software that automatically handles boring paperwork and setup tasks when you start a business.
stories.why_it_matters: If this tool works well, small-business owners might save time on paperwork in the future — but right now this is mostly a business investment story.

stories.title: OpenAI is giving ChatGPT free users unlimited text chats
stories.simple_summary: OpenAI is removing limits on how many times free ChatGPT users can chat with the AI each day.
stories.why_it_matters: If you use the free version of ChatGPT, you'll have fewer frustrations with the service restricting your use.

stories.title: Gen Z dating apps like Ditto ditch swiping in favor of AI matchmaking
stories.simple_summary: Young dating apps are replacing the swipe system (like Tinder) with AI that tries to match people based on what they like instead of just photos.
stories.why_it_matters: If you or someone you know uses dating apps, these new ones might work better than endless swiping — but this only matters if you're actually looking to date.

stories.title: OpenAI says Apple’s own security practices undermine its trade secrets case
stories.simple_summary: OpenAI is defending itself in a lawsuit from Apple by arguing that Apple's own security practices weren't strong enough to protect secret information.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly matters to investors and legal watchers — the outcome of tech company lawsuits generally doesn't affect everyday people.

stories.title: SoftBank donated $50 million to Trump’s library months before federal data center deal
stories.simple_summary: Japanese company SoftBank donated $50 million to the Trump Presidential Library in January, then a few months later announced it would lease federal land to build a large data center in Ohio.
stories.why_it_matters: This raises questions about whether political donations influence business deals with the government — it's something to be aware of when big companies get favorable government treatment.

stories.title: The left and right agree on one thing: no data centers
stories.simple_summary: Communities across the country, both in Democratic and Republican areas, are opposing new data center construction because they're concerned about environmental and community impacts.
stories.why_it_matters: If you live near where a data center might be built, local resistance might prevent it — but if you don't, this probably doesn't affect you directly.

stories.title: Amid legal battles, Suno says it will start watermarking songs
stories.simple_summary: Suno, an AI music creation company that's facing lawsuits, says it will add watermarks to its songs to show they were made by AI.
stories.why_it_matters: This is mostly important for the legal disputes between AI companies and musicians — most people won't notice the difference.
